extra_documents.TRADEMARKS.md:
# Trademarks

This repository mentions real companies, products and organisations in a few places, most of all in the colour
library under `skills/brand-identity/assets/library/` (colours read from public websites, with the brand's name and
site). Every such name, logo, trade dress and colour belongs to its owner. Nothing here is affiliated with, sponsored
by or endorsed by any of them.

## What the data is

- Colours are **approximations of what a site's CSS rendered on the day it was measured**. They are not the owners'
  brand specifications, and they drift whenever the site changes.
- The library is **reference material**: it shows which hues and lightness patterns a sector already uses, so a new
  identity can find open space. It is named and used for that purpose only.
- Font names (for example Google Fonts families) are used to identify the typefaces. Each family keeps its own
  licence, which the skill checks and states in its output.

## What the licence does not give you

- The MIT licence covers this repository's code and original writing. It transfers **no rights** in any third-party
  name, logo, colour or trade dress.
- The skill is built to steer away from imitation: it is told to look for what a category leaves unclaimed and never
  to copy a competitor's identity. Do not use another company's colours, marks or type treatment to suggest a link
  with that company.
- The skill cannot clear a mark or a colour for registration. Protection depends on the jurisdiction and on how a
  mark is used. If a trademark search matters for your brand, ask a trademark professional.
- Pantone and other proprietary colour systems are named only where the user supplies a reference. None of their
  data is distributed here.

## Fictional examples

The briefs in `evals/fixtures/` and the example brands shown in this repository use invented businesses.
Any likeness to a real business is accidental.

## Removal requests

If you own one of the marks and want an entry taken out, open an issue and it will be removed promptly.

## colormason (vladzima/colormason), MIT

Used in `skills/brand-identity/scripts/palette_build.py` and `colorlib.py`: the approach of a fixed OKLCH lightness
ladder with a chroma taper toward both ends, a binary search for the largest in-gamut chroma at a given lightness and
hue, and the contrast auto-fix that moves a failing role to another step of the *same* ramp and reports the move.
Changed here: the brand hex is kept verbatim at its anchor step (colormason's ramps drop it), the ladder bends around
the seed, chroma follows the hue's own max-chroma curve, and hue-offset templates are not the default.

## color-harmony (katkurigopi05/color-harmony), MIT

Used in `skills/brand-identity/scripts/palette_audit.py`: role-labelled findings, a minimal-change `suggested_fix` per
finding, and a non-zero exit status when a blocking check fails. Changed here: CIEDE2000 instead of deltaE 76,
WCAG 2 contrast for every role pair used together in both modes, colour-vision-deficiency simulation, no HSL
"gap zone" harmony scoring.

    Copyright (c) 2026 katkurigopi05

    (MIT License, same permission notice and disclaimer as above.)

## Published constants and reference data

- **OKLab matrices**: Björn Ottosson, "A perceptual color space for image processing" (2020, matrices revised
  2021-01-25), <https://bottosson.github.io/posts/oklab/>; the reference code is offered as public domain / MIT.
- **sRGB/XYZ and Bradford matrices, gamut-mapping algorithm, deltaE OK**: CSS Color Module Level 4, W3C,
  <https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color-4/>. Sample code © W3C, W3C Software and Document License.
- **Colour-vision-deficiency matrices**: Machado, Oliveira & Fernandes 2009 (protan/deutan, severity 1.0),
  <https://www.inf.ufrgs.br/~oliveira/pubs_files/CVD_Simulation/CVD_Simulation.html>; Brettel, Viénot & Mollon 1997
  tritan matrices as precomputed by libDaltonLens (public domain), <https://github.com/DaltonLens/libDaltonLens>.
- **CIEDE2000 test data** (in `tests/test_colorlib.py`): Sharma, Wu & Dalal 2005, "The CIEDE2000 color-difference
  formula: implementation notes, supplementary test data, and mathematical observations", Color Res Appl 30:21-30.
- **Lightness ladder medians and neutral-chroma shape** (`palette_build.py` `LADDER`, `NEUTRAL_LADDER`,
  `NEUTRAL_CHROMA_SHAPE`): measured from the Tailwind CSS v4 default theme (`theme.css`), Copyright (c) Tailwind Labs,
  Inc., MIT License, <https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss>. Only derived numbers are used, no source.

## Dembrandt (dembrandt/dembrandt), MIT

Used in `skills/brand-identity/scripts/site/site_engine.js` and `scripts/site_palette.py` as a reference for
heuristics only (no code): reading colours from computed styles of the rendered page, `:root` custom properties as a
token layer, button/CTA backgrounds as a strong primary signal, an accent at least 30° of hue away from primary,
hiding known consent platforms by selector. Changed here: consent banners are hidden, never clicked (read-only), and
the site is recoloured rather than only measured.

    Copyright (c) 2025 thevangelist

    (MIT License, same permission notice and disclaimer as above.)

## GF Latin Core codepoint list, Apache-2.0

Used in `skills/brand-identity/assets/fonts/gf-latin-core.txt`: the GF Latin Core codepoint list from google/glyphsets
(https://github.com/googlefonts/glyphsets, commit 432104e), Copyright Google LLC and the glyphsets authors, Apache
License 2.0 (full text below). Read as an informational coverage check only.

## Language data from gflanguages (googlefonts/lang), Apache-2.0

`skills/brand-identity/assets/languages.json.gz` is exported by `tools/export_languages.py` from the gflanguages
Python package (version recorded in the file; https://github.com/googlefonts/lang), Copyright Google LLC, Apache
License 2.0. Only these fields are kept: per language its id, name, population, historical flag and the base,
auxiliary and punctuation exemplar characters; per script its name. gflanguages adapts its exemplar characters
from the Unicode Common Locale Data Repository (CLDR, https://cldr.unicode.org/), Copyright © 1991-2026 Unicode,
Inc., Unicode License v3 (full text below). Used by the font audit's language coverage check.

## Playwright (microsoft/playwright), Apache-2.0

`skills/brand-identity/scripts/cdplib.py`: the in-page screenshot preparation script `_PREPARE` (finish or cancel CSS
animations, hide carets, undo afterwards) is adapted from Playwright's `inPagePrepareForScreenshots`
(`packages/playwright-core/src/server/screenshotter.ts`); changed here: type annotations dropped, the code condensed
into one expression evaluated over CDP. The rest of `cdplib.py` re-implements, without copying source, other behaviour
of playwright-core 1.63: the Chrome command-line switches and default font families for headless Chromium
(configuration values), the order of the DevTools calls that set up a page, the network-idle rule (500 ms per frame)
and the window listeners its injected script registers. Apache License 2.0 (full text below),
https://github.com/microsoft/playwright.

# Credits

Every imported asset gets a line here: what it is, where it came from, who made
it, and the licence. Delete the examples once real rows are in.

| Asset | File | Source | Author | Licence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| hero fighter rig (skinned) | `assets/knight.glb` | https://poly.pizza/m/xxxx | @author | CC0 |
| stall awning texture | `assets/awning.glb` | https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/xxxx | @author | CC-BY 4.0 |
| crow animation clips | `assets/crow.anim.glb` | user-supplied | — | owned by client |

## Rules

- **Allowed:** CC0, public domain, CC-BY with attribution, assets the user owns
  or supplied, and AI-generated meshes the user commissioned (Meshy, Tripo, etc).
- **Not allowed without asking:** anything NC, ND, "editorial use only", ripped
  from a game, or with no stated licence. Ask the user; do not guess.
- CC-BY needs visible attribution in the page footer or an `About` line, not just
  this file.

# Water harness

A working scene for `water.js`, `wake.js` and `splash.js`, and a worked example
of the QA loop. No story, no cast: two swimmers crossing a pool on a sine, a
timed splash, and the post pass.

```bash
npm i three esbuild playwright-core     # or link a project that already has them
node build.mjs                          # dist/app.js + index.html
python3 -m http.server 4181 &
BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4181/index.html QA_DIR=shots SHOTS="1.75:splash" \
  node ../../templates/qa/shoot.mjs     # copy the qa folder into the root first
```

## What the verification found

- `water.js` is sound: the vertex ramp reads as depth provided the pool's shallow
  to deep axis matches the plane's local X, and the basin under it is dark. A deck
  box spanning the whole slab puts beige under the water and the surface reads as
  a stain, which is a scene bug, not an effect bug.
- `wake.js` works; rings are pooled and one `spawn` tick is shared by every
  swimmer, so more than four bodies will exhaust the ring pool.
- `splash.js` used `Math.random` in `trigger`, so two identical frames never
  matched. It now takes a `burstSeed`. Both effects also gained `reset()`: they
  integrate `dt`, so freezing the clock does not reset them, and a frozen frame
  showed the last played state. Re-simulating from zero in fixed steps took a
  two-frame diff from 334 differing pixels to 18.
